DECISION GATE (a) RESOLVED — version bump chosen, with a partition rule rather than a migration. Implementation is on branch fix/write-primitives-catalog-v2, worktree BenchBox.wt-write-primitives-catalog-v2, published as PR 2342 onto develop.

Rule recorded: results are partitioned by catalog version and the partitions are not comparable. A version-1 bundle compares only to other version-1 bundles and is excluded from version-2 aggregates. Version-1 measurements are never rewritten or transformed, because the underlying SQL differs; re-running the benchmark is the migration path. Version 1 and version 2 measure different work — under version 1 a cloud engine received baseline SQL it often could not execute, so operations that previously errored now run.

Independently verified during takeover: catalog version 1 to 2; benchmark _version "1.0" to "2.0"; 136 operations before and after with none added or removed and exactly 86 modified; 75 of those only gained cloud platform_overrides; 11 changed their base write_sql. Those 11 affect every platform, not just cloud, so they were executed against real DuckDB under both catalogs: all 11 pass under both, no regression. 51 DuckDB end-to-end write-primitives integration tests pass under both catalogs.

Corpus check: no write-primitives bundle exists in results-data on develop or published-results, so nothing needs re-labeling. Three retained migration manifests reference fourteen write-primitives bundles from May 2026 that are no longer in the corpus; if restored they belong to the version-1 partition.

REVIEW DEFECTS RESOLVED (commit d58a7ef2a on the same branch). Two P1 findings from the PR reviewer were confirmed against vendor documentation and fixed, not rebutted.

1. Decimal truncation. The 11 base-SQL changes included unparameterized CAST(x AS NUMERIC) building four DECIMAL(15,2) line-item columns in insert_batch_values_100 and insert_batch_values_1000. Snowflake resolves bare NUMERIC to NUMBER with scale 0 and Databricks resolves bare DECIMAL to DECIMAL(10,0), so the 0.05 discount and 0.02 tax constants truncated to zero before reaching their columns. Count-only validation hid this, so both operations reported success on semantically wrong rows. Fixed by naming the scale explicitly, CAST(x AS DECIMAL(15,2)), in the base SQL and in the snowflake and databricks overrides for both variants. Reproduced the truncation directly: CAST(0.05 AS DECIMAL(10,0)) gives 0, CAST(0.05 AS DECIMAL(15,2)) gives 0.05. Corrected catalog SQL run against DuckDB returns discount=0.05 and tax=0.02 for all 100 and all 1000 rows. BigQuery deliberately keeps the bare form: its NUMERIC already has scale 9 and it forbids parameterized types in CAST, which are valid only for columns and script variables. A regression test pins the explicit scale per override source and pins the BigQuery difference.

2. BigQuery cleanup asymmetry. update_date_arithmetic and merge_date_arithmetic gained a BigQuery write override spelling date arithmetic as DATE_ADD(..., INTERVAL 7 DAY), because BigQuery requires an INT64 expression for a single-part interval literal and rejects the quoted INTERVAL '7' DAY in the base SQL. The matching cleanup_sql still used the quoted form, and cleanup goes straight to connection.execute with no override resolution and no rewrite pass. Since success and status derive only from validation_passed, the write would have succeeded while cleanup failed and was recorded merely as a warning, leaving rows date-shifted and still marked for later operations to measure. No interval spelling is valid on both BigQuery and the engines requiring the quoted form, and DuckDB accepting both is the only engine verified to do so, so both operations are now marked unsupported on BigQuery. This is not a coverage regression: on develop they have no bigquery key at all, so the base SQL ran and failed on the same quoted literal. The PR had converted a loud failure into a silent write/cleanup split; the null override restores the loud, structured one. Verified at runtime that both return status=SKIPPED on BigQuery and execute zero SQL.

The durable fix for finding 2 is cleanup SQL gaining the same override resolution write SQL already has. That is an executor change and belongs with the loader work, not a catalog version bump.
